title: Quality of recovery after arthroscopic meniscectomy with remimazolam or propofol anesthesia: A randomized controlled trial
content:
by Eunah Cho, Ha Yan Kim, Yangjin Kim, Seokyung Shin

Background

Anesthetic technique may influence postoperative quality of recovery (QoR). Remimazolam may offer hemodynamic stability and favorable early recovery characteristics, but its effect on patient-reported QoR compared with propofol remains unclear. This is particularly relevant in minor orthopedic surgery, where QoR is a principal outcome. This randomized controlled trial compared postoperative QoR between propofol-based and remimazolam-based total intravenous anesthesia (TIVA) using the QoR-40 questionnaire.

Materials and methods

Eighty adult patients undergoing elective arthroscopic meniscectomy were randomly assigned to propofol-based or remimazolam-based TIVA; 71 patients completed the QoR-40 questionnaire and were included in the final analysis (36 in the Propofol group, 35 in the Remimazolam group). The primary outcome was the global QoR-40 score on postoperative day (POD) 1. Secondary outcomes included intraoperative hemodynamic variables, anesthetic and analgesic requirements, postoperative recovery profiles, pain scores, and postoperative nausea and vomiting.

Results

Global QoR-40 scores on POD 1 did not differ significantly between the Propofol and Remimazolam groups (166.1 ± 16.8 vs. 170.6 ± 13.6; mean difference −4.5, 95% CI −11.8 to 2.7; P = 0.218). In an exploratory analysis, the emotional-state domain scores were higher in the Remimazolam group (37.0 ± 4.3 vs. 39.2 ± 2.5; mean difference −2.2, 95% CI −3.9 to −0.6; P = 0.009). The Remimazolam group had a longer time to full alertness (18 [15–24] vs. 37 [31–45] min; P < 0.001) and longer post-anesthesia care unit stay (30 [30–39] vs. 38 [30–50] min; P = 0.008). Intraoperative hypotension requiring ephedrine occurred more frequently in the Propofol group (44.4% vs. 17.1%; P = 0.013).

Conclusions

Global QoR-40 scores on POD 1 did not differ significantly between propofol-based and remimazolam-based TIVA in adults undergoing elective arthroscopic meniscectomy, although remimazolam was associated with greater intraoperative hemodynamic stability at the cost of slower return to full alertness.
